summary: FAT32 written by the kernel from a program, across reboots, through a crash and its repair, from BusyBox and by two writers under the lag device, judged on the host by mkfatfixture's walk, mtools and fsck.fat; the program is tests/cases/machine/fswrite_scenario.c

cases.behavior: FAT32 written from a program and unmounted, judged on the host by the walk, mtools and the external checker, read back after a reboot, ended in the middle of a write sequence and checked by the next writable mount, then written from BusyBox at a bounded count of disk commands; each boot carries the volume the one before it left

execution.cleanup: libetude-case ends the machines and removes the disk's copy, which it keeps after a failure; the scenario removes the files it reads out of the volume once they are judged the same

steps.does: boot the test image on the disk's copy and run fatwriteprobe write at the debug shell, then end the machine with QMP's quit
walk the volume with mkfatfixture --check, read pattern.bin and list the names with mtools, and run the external checker over a copy of the volume
boot the test image again and run fatwriteprobe readback, then end the machine with QMP's quit
boot the test image, run fatwriteprobe crash and end the machine with QMP's quit once it says FATWRITE WRITING
read the dirty flag of the volume the killed machine left, with mkfatfixture --check
boot the test image and run fatwriteprobe repair, whose writable mount checks the volume, then end the machine with QMP's quit
walk the repaired volume and keep its line of lost clusters
boot os-real, log in as root at the console, mount the volume, copy, move, write and remove on it with BusyBox, write and remove 4 MiB between readings of /proc/disk, and unmount it
walk the volume, read the copied program on the host and compare it with os-real's /bin/busybox

assertions.checks: fatwriteprobe write exits 0 after FATWRITE OK (wrote): it mounted the volume, wrote pattern.bin, a long-named file, a directory and a file in it, a renamed, a removed and an fsynced file, and unmounted the volume
mkfatfixture --check finds the written volume consistent, its dirty flag aside
mcopy reads pattern.bin as 65536 bytes, byte i being (i * 31 + 7) mod 256
mdir lists pattern.bin, Long Name File.txt, Sub Dir, renamed.txt and synced.txt, and not gone.txt
fsck.fat -n calls a copy of the written volume clean
fatwriteprobe readback exits 0 after FATWRITE OK (read back) on the next boot: every byte and name, the long name with its case folded and its short alias, the renamed and removed names gone
fatwriteprobe crash says FATWRITE WRITING once the first file of its sequence is written
the volume the machine ended in the middle of the write sequence left has the dirty flag set, as the walk reports it
fatwriteprobe repair exits 0 after FATWRITE OK (repaired): the writable mount after the crash keeps a file of the sequence and unmounts
that mount's records say vfat: check: the volume was not unmounted cleanly, and vfat: check: consistent
the walk finds the repaired volume consistent, its dirty flag and the lost clusters that the crash may leave and the mount's check leaves aside

BusyBox on os-real mounts the volume as vfat, copies /bin/busybox onto it, makes a directory, moves the copy into it as Busy Box, writes a file, removes renamed.txt, and cmp finds the copy's bytes the same
dd writes a file of 4 MiB in 64 KiB calls and sync returns, and stat gives its size, 4194304
the 4 MiB write and its sync take disk commands, fewer than 5000 by /proc/disk, since the FAT entries of a run are written a 4 KiB block at a time
the file's removal and its sync take disk commands, fewer than 256 by /proc/disk
umount of the volume succeeds
the walk finds the volume consistent after BusyBox, its dirty flag and the repaired walk's lost clusters aside
mcopy reads d/Busy Box as the bytes of os-real's /bin/busybox, which readfile.krffs takes out of the image

progress.means: a step of the manifest has ended

native.reason: the case ends a machine in the middle of a write sequence and reads the disk it left on the host between boots

cases.behavior: two writers and a sync at once on FAT32 under the lag device, on a fresh copy of the disk, each file whole and the volume consistent

execution.cleanup: libetude-case ends the machine and removes the disk's copy, which it keeps after a failure

steps.does: boot the test image with the lag device over disk 0, the disk's flushes kept from the host, and run lagprobe writers at the debug shell, then end the machine with QMP's quit

assertions.checks: lagprobe writers exits 0 after LAGPROBE OK: two children write a file each while the parent syncs the volume twenty times, every sync returns 0, each file reads back as its own bytes, and the volume unmounts
mkfatfixture --check finds the volume consistent, its dirty flag aside

progress.means: a step of the manifest has ended

timing.assumes: the lag device answers each request of disk 0's partitions three kernel ticks late as the stimulus, so that the requests of the writers and the sync interleave; the case judges the files and the volume they leave, never elapsed time
sleep_ms, through which the parent spaces its syncs 30 ms apart across the writers' run, as the stimulus; the probe judges each file's bytes and every sync's result, never elapsed time

native.reason: the lag device over disk 0 is set on the kernel's boot line
